Article Title: UPI gets festive boost: Digital payments hit a record 24.51 billion transactions in August
Article Text:
Digital payments hit a record 24.51 billion transactions in August

Festive activity adds to UPI momentum

From 1.78 crore transactions to 24,162 crore

UPI now accepted in 11 countries

Unified Payments Interface (UPI) hit a new monthly high in August, with transaction volumes crossing 24 billion for the first time in a month and reaching 24.51 billion, according to data released by the National Payments Corporation of India (NPCI) on Tuesday.The record came as transaction activity picked up during the festive period, particularly around Raksha Bandhan. UPI processed transactions worth Rs 29.82 lakh crore during the month, taking the value close to the record Rs 29.9 lakh crore recorded in May and July 2026.The August volume was 22% higher than the 19.63 billion transactions recorded in the same month last year. It also marked a rise from 23.66 billion transactions in July, 22.72 billion in June and 23.2 billion in May.In value terms, August transactions were up 20% from Rs 24.85 lakh crore a year earlier.The rise in transaction volumes in August was further supported by Raksha Bandhan, which led to higher peer-to-peer (P2P) transfers and small-ticket gifting, Cashfree Payments co-founder Reeju Datta said."The volume growth in August was further bolstered by festive activity such as Raksha Bandhan, which naturally drove a surge in everyday peer-to-peer (P2P) transfers and small-ticket gifting, and consistent aggregate transaction value with an increase in volume over the past three months underscores the expanding reach and depth of the UPI ecosystem," Cashfree Payments co-founder Reeju Datta said.Datta said the upcoming festive season presented an exciting growth frontier.Network People Services Technologies (NPST) co-founder and CEO Deepak Chand Thakur said the next phase of growth would come as newer UPI use cases develop."As the festive season approaches and new use cases such as credit on UPI start to mature, continued investment in resilient, intelligent infrastructure will be key to sustaining India's leadership in digital payments, Network People Services Technologies (NPST) co-founder and CEO Deepak Chand Thakur said.The latest monthly record comes as UPI continues to expand rapidly since its launch on August 25, 2016.Its annual transaction volume has grown from 1.78 crore in 2016-17 to more than 24,162 crore in 2025-26, an almost 13,000-fold increase.Transaction value has also climbed sharply over the decade, from Rs 0.07 lakh crore in FY17 to around Rs 314 lakh crore in FY26 — an increase of more than 4,000 times.The growth trajectory reached another milestone in May 2026, when monthly UPI transactions crossed 2,300 crore for the first time. The month recorded 2,320 crore transactions.UPI's expansion has also extended beyond India. The payment system is now accepted in 11 countries, with Uzbekistan the latest addition.The other countries where UPI is accepted are Singapore, the United Arab Emirates, France, Mauritius, Nepal, Bhutan, Qatar, Sri Lanka, Cambodia, and Greece.NPCI, an initiative of the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) and the Indian Banks' Association (IBA), is the umbrella organisation for operating retail payments and settlement systems in India. It runs UPI, which enables real-time payments between peers and at merchants' end while making purchases.
Article Summary: Digital payments hit a record 24.51 billion transactions in August. Record came as transaction activity picked up during the festive period. UPI processed transactions worth Rs 29.82 lakh crore during the month. The payment system is now accepted in 11 countries, with Uzbekistan the latest addition.

Article Title: Oil prices jump 1% as US-Iran strikes deepen fears of supply disruption
Article Text:
The price nears $96 a barrel as US-Iran strikes stoke fears of supply disruption

Oil prices extended their sharp rally on Wednesday, rising nearly 1 per cent in early trade as the latest US-Iran military escalation heightened fears that disruptions to crude supplies could worsen.Brent crude futures rose 87 cents, or 0.92 per cent, to $95.52 a barrel by 0008 GMT, while US West Texas Intermediate crude gained 80 cents, or 0.89 per cent, to $91.02. The move came after both benchmarks surged more than $4 on Tuesday. Brent recorded its biggest daily gain since July 24, while WTI posted its strongest rise since July 23.A key concern for oil markets is the Strait of Hormuz, through which around one-fifth of the world's oil consumption passed before the conflict. Iran has effectively shut the waterway to commercial shipping, while attacks on two tankers leaving the strait on Monday have already forced traders to seek alternative crude supplies.The latest US-Iran exchange has raised the risk of further disruption. The United States said it carried out a series of overnight airstrikes against targets in Iran, while Tehran responded with attacks on US military positions across the region.US Central Command said the strikes followed attempted attacks by Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) on commercial shipping in the Strait of Hormuz and US personnel in the region.The IRGC warned that the US strikes would further restrict traffic through the strategic waterway. It also said Iran had targeted a US base in Jordan with ballistic missiles. Iranian state media separately reported a large-scale drone attack on a US base in Bahrain.Jordan said its air defences intercepted 10 of 13 ballistic missiles that entered its airspace. Two US officials said there were no reported American casualties from the attacks so far, while Kuwait said its armed forces were dealing with hostile drone activity.The escalation follows a weekend flare-up in fighting, the first since July, adding to uncertainty over the security of oil shipments from the region.US inventory data provided another source of support for crude prices. Oil stocks in the world's largest producer fell by 2.6 million barrels in the week ended August 28, while distillate inventories, including diesel and heating oil, declined by 265,000 barrels, according to market sources citing American Petroleum Institute data.
Article Summary: Brent crude futures rose 87 cents, or 0.92 per cent, to $95.52 a barrel. US West Texas Intermediate crude gained 80 cents to $91.02. The move came after both benchmarks surged more than $4 on Tuesday.

Article Title: Centre halves sugar stock limit for dealers to curb hoarding, price rise
Article Text: NEW DELHI: Centre on Tuesday tightened the stock limit for sugar dealers, reducing it from 4,000 quintals to 2,000 quintals from September 15 to November 30, as it sought to curb hoarding and contain rising retail prices.The food ministry said the existing 4,000-quintal limit would continue in Kolkata and its extended metropolitan areas “considering the specific market requirements of the region”.The move is aimed at ensuring adequate availability of sugar in the domestic market and preventing hoarding and speculative trading, the ministry said.Under the revised rules, dealers cannot hold sugar stocks for more than 30 days from the date of receipt. They will also not be allowed to hold more than 2,000 quintals at any time at any location across the country.The ministry said the 4,000-quintal limit would remain in place in Kolkata because the region sources sugar mainly from Uttar Pradesh and Maharashtra and supplies it to eastern and northeastern states.The decision comes as sugar prices remain elevated. The all-India average retail price stood at Rs 63.28 per kg on August 31, up 37% from Rs 46.02 per kg a year earlier, according to Consumer Affairs Ministry data.Wholesale prices also rose 36.28% year-on-year to Rs 58.40 per kg. However, industry data showed some easing in mill-level prices. The ex-mill price of sugar in Maharashtra fell to Rs 45-46 per kg on September 1 from a peak of Rs 67 per kg on August 18.The Centre has accused sugar mills of “jacking up” prices, while maintaining that the country has adequate stocks, PTI reported.The government’s position comes despite sugar production estimates for the 2025-26 marketing year, which runs from October to September, being revised down to 306 lakh tonnes from the earlier estimate of 343 lakh tonnes.
Article Summary: The existing 4,000-quintal limit would continue in Kolkata and its extended metropolitan areas. The all-India average retail price stood at Rs 63.28 per kg on August 31, up 37% from Rs 46.02 per kg a year earlier.

Article Title: Gold pledged for loan stolen in bank robbery: Borrower gets gold value plus Rs 88,362 for making charges and stones, Rs 40,000 compensation - how he won the case
Article Text:
The jewellery remained in the custody of the bank branch but was subsequently robbed, according to the bank’s submission. (Image for representative purpose only)

Pledged gold jewellery stolen : What exactly happened

For the first loan account, the bank valued the gold at Rs 2600/g and paid Rs 1,56,033 towards the gold value, based on a net gold weight of 90 grams.

Under the second loan account, the jewellery had a gross weight of 133 grams and a net weight of 85 grams. The Canara Bank branch valued the gold at Rs 2500/g and paid the borrower around Rs 2,12,500.

What did the District Commission rule?

Bank challenges ruling

Why the State Commission ruled in favour of the borrower

Rs 88,362 along with 9% interest

Rs 30,000 as compensation

Rs 10,000 towards litigation expenses

Imagine this case: You have taken a loan against your gold. That gold is lying with the bank. Then in a bank robbery the gold is stolen. Who is responsible for the loss? Who pays? In one such case, a man challenged the bank and won the case.The issue was eventually considered by a consumer commission, which delivered a ruling on how the value of jewellery lost while in a bank’s custody should be settled.So, what happens if gold jewellery pledged against a gold loan is stolen from the bank? For a borrower, the loss can raise a bigger question than simply recovering the value of the gold. Should the bank pay only for the metal, or should the compensation also cover making charges and the value of stones?A Tumkur resident in Karnataka faced this very situation and chose to challenge the bank’s settlement.The Tumkur resident had opened two gold loan accounts with a Canara Bank branch in August 2017. He pledged two gold items against each loan account, according to an ET report. The jewellery pledged under the first account weighed 120.80 grams, while that under the second weighed 133 grams. He borrowed Rs 1,50,000 against each account.The jewellery remained in the custody of the Canara Bank branch but was subsequently robbed, according to the bank’s submission, the report said.After discovering that the gold articles had been stolen, the bank wrote to the borrower on July 26, 2018, offering to pay him the value of the gold.The borrower, however, sought an additional amount to account for the jewellery’s making charges and stone value. He claimed 20% towards making charges and 3% for the stone value, seeking a further payment of Rs 88,362.He then approached the District Commission, alleging deficiency in service and unfair trade practice.Jayesh H, Co - Founder at Juris Corp told ET that determining the appropriate compensation in such cases can be a matter of debate, particularly over whether the borrower should receive the market value, replacement value or the actual cost incurred by the pledgor.“The bank’s liability is almost absolute in such cases. As regards awarding, making charges etc., even if not from replacement value perspective, it’s equally applicable as regards costs incurred by the pledgor.”He said a complainant should be in a position to establish the total costs incurred in relation to the jewellery.After hearing the case, the District Commission allowed the complaint in July 2020.It directed the bank to pay the additional amount claimed by the borrower, along with Rs 30,000 as compensation and Rs 10,000 towards litigation expenses, within 45 days.The commission noted that the borrower had alleged that the bank had not paid the 20% making charges and 3% stone value and had refused to settle the remaining amount. After considering the facts and circumstances, it ordered the lender to pay an additional Rs 88,362, along with 9% interest from 29.08.2018.The bank then challenged the District Commission’s decision before the Karnataka State Disputes Redressal Commission.Canara Bank argued that it was not responsible for paying the additional amount contending that there was no deficiency in service since it had already paid the value of the 85 grams of gold.“The complainant, without any documents, is demanding payment of 20% making charges and 3% stone value; the same cannot be payable. The net value of the gold was already paid, but the District Commission failed to appreciate the said facts and allowed this appeal,” it said.The bank further argued that the District Commission’s order was not legally sustainable and that there had been no deficiency in service. It therefore asked the State Commission to set aside the District Commission’s order.The Karnataka State Disputes Redressal Commission rejected Canara Bank’s appeal and upheld the District Commission’s order. "We are of the opinion that the order passed by the District Commission is in accordance with law," the State Commission stated.The commission emphasised that when jewellery kept in a bank’s custody is lost through robbery or theft, the bank has a duty to settle its value at the prevailing rates. This value, it said, should include both the making charges and the value of the stones.The State Commission also held that the bank cannot insist on an invoice as proof that making charges had been imposed on the jewellery. It noted that making charges are levied on gold ornaments as a matter of course and are therefore payable.“If the ornaments which are in the custody of the Appellant Bank were lost either by way of robbery or by theft, it is bound on duty on the Bank to settle the value of the Gold Ornaments at prevailing rates, which includes the making charges and also stone value,” the Karnataka States Disputes Redressal Commission said.Accordingly, the Canara Bank branch was directed to pay the borrower:
Article Summary: Gold jewellery pledged against a gold loan is stolen from the bank. For a borrower, the loss can raise a bigger question than simply recovering the value of the gold. Should the bank pay only for the metal, or should the compensation also cover making charges and value of stones?

Article Title: Mobile shop owner won Rs 15 lakh chit prize but waited 55 days for payout; company blamed late sureties, but consumer commission found its records contradicted the claim and ordered Rs 44,500 relief
Article Text:
The dispute was not about the eligibility for the chit prize or whether the claimant had won the bid.

Rs 15 lakh chit prize delay case: How the mobile shop owner won

Company said sureties were submitted late

Commission finds more than 55-day delay

Rs 1,100 interest found too little

Rs 17,500 insurance amount also in dispute

Consumer commission upholds order

Won a chit prize but the payout is delayed? A Telangana consumer commission has upheld an order against Kapil Chits after holding the company responsible for delaying the payment of a Rs 15 lakh chit prize for more than 55 days. Kapil Chits attributed the delay to late submission of sureties, but the commission found the company records revealing otherwise.The dispute was not about the eligibility for the chit prize or whether the claimant had won the bid. The Commission had already accepted that he was the successful bidder. The question before it was how much time Kapil Chits could reasonably take to release the Rs 15 lakh prize amount the requirement for furnishing the necessary sureties was fulfilled.The amount was payable to S. Eashwar, a mobile shop owner from Mahabubnagar who had emerged as the successful bidder in a Rs 25 lakh chit.S. Eashwar, a self-employed mobile shop owner from Mahabubnagar, had subscribed to a Rs 25 lakh chit run by Kapil Chits.The chit commenced in May 2018, and Eashwar was required to contribute Rs 50,000 every month for 50 months. He had joined the scheme with the intention of using the prize money to expand his mobile business.At the chit auction conducted on December 15, 2018, Eashwar emerged as the successful bidder after agreeing to forgo Rs 10 lakh. As a result, the prize amount payable to him was Rs 15 lakh.Eashwar subsequently submitted the four sureties sought by the chit company. Among those provided as sureties were three income-tax payers and a head nurse employed at a government hospital.Kapil Chits attributed the delay to Eashwar’s late submission of the required sureties, saying the documents had to be verified before the prize money could be released. The Telangana State Consumer Commission, however, found that the company’s own records showed the sureties had been submitted on March 28, 2019. It therefore concluded that the payment of the prize amount had been delayed by more than 55 days, according to an ET report.The disagreement centred on the time taken by Kapil Chits to release Eashwar’s prize money.Kapil Chits maintained that Eashwar had submitted the required sureties only on April 28, 2019. According to the company, the documents first had to go through verification before the prize amount could be released, and the payment was ultimately made on May 18.The company further contended that, after the verification was completed, the delay was limited to five days. It said it had already paid Rs 1,100 as interest for this period.The Telangana State Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission, however, found that the company’s own records did not support this version of events.The Commission pointed to a document submitted by Kapil Chits showing that the sureties had in fact been furnished by Eashwar on March 28, 2019, a month earlier than the date claimed by the company.It also recorded that the final payment of Rs 13,00,375 was made only on May 25, 2019. Overall, Kapil Chits paid Eashwar Rs 14,85,000 in three separate instalments.The Telangana State Consumer Commission noted that the Chit Fund Act does not lay down a specific deadline for a chit fund company to release the prize amount after receiving the required sureties.However, the absence of a prescribed time limit did not give the company the liberty to keep the payment pending indefinitely.The Commission held that even if seven days were allowed for verifying the sureties, the prize amount should have been paid by April 1, 2019.Instead, the final instalment was released only on May 25.The Commission consequently calculated the delay at more than 55 days and held that the payment had not been made within a reasonable period.It therefore concurred with the District Consumer Commission’s finding that the delay constituted a deficiency in service.Kapil Chits defended its position by pointing out that it had already paid Rs 1,100 as interest for the delay in releasing the prize money.The State Commission, however, did not consider this amount sufficient in view of the length of the delay.It observed that calculating interest on the Rs 15 lakh prize amount at 12% per annum for a period of two months would result in an amount of around Rs 30,000.The interest actually paid by the company, at Rs 1,100, was substantially lower than this figure.The Commission consequently upheld the District Commission’s decision to grant Rs 25,000 as compensation for the delayed payment.Eashwar had raised another issue, alleging that Kapil Chits had deducted Rs 17,500 from his chit amount towards an insurance premium without obtaining his consent.The company disputed this claim, stating that the amount had subsequently been returned to Eashwar. It also relied on documents in support of its position.Despite this, the District Commission ordered Kapil Chits to refund the Rs 17,500. It also directed the company to pay Rs 25,000 as compensation for the delay and Rs 2,000 towards the costs of the proceedings.Kapil Chits then challenged the District Commission’s order before the Telangana State Consumer Commission.After reviewing the records and the submissions, the Telangana State Consumer Commission found no grounds to alter the District Commission’s decision regarding the delayed payment.The State Commission noted that the documents on record established that Eashwar had furnished the sureties on March 28, while the final payment was made only on May 25.It accordingly upheld the Rs 25,000 compensation awarded for the delay, along with Rs 2,000 towards litigation costs and the direction to refund Rs 17,500. Together, these amounts took the total monetary relief awarded to Eashwar to Rs 44,500.The Telangana State Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission, Hyderabad, passed the order on August 19, 2026.
Article Summary: S. Eashwar, a self-employed mobile shop owner from Mahabubnagar, had subscribed to a Rs 25 lakh chit run by Kapil Chits. The dispute was not about the eligibility for the chit prize or whether the claimant had won the bid. The disagreement centred on the time taken by Kapill Chits to release Eashwar’s prize money.

Article Title: Start with Rs 25,000 basic salary, end with Rs 1 crore corpus: How EPF compounding math can make you a crorepati at 8.25% interest in less than 30 years with 6% annual increment
Article Text:
Over time, the interest earned on the accumulated balance earns interest, allowing compounding to steadily increase your retirement savings.

EPF math: How compounding can take you past Rs 1 crore

To see how an EPF corpus of Rs 1 crore could be accumulated, consider an employee with a basic salary of Rs 25,000 a month. For the purpose of this calculation based on SBI Securities calculator, the employee’s EPF contribution is taken as 12% of basic wages.

That calculator assumes an employer contribution to EPF at 3.67% since out of the employer’s 12% contribution, 8.33% goes towards the Employee Pension Scheme Account.

Particulars Details Basic salary Rs 25,000 per month EPF interest rate 8.25% Employee EPF contribution 12% Investment period 29 years Annual salary increase 6% Total EPF contributions Rs 34,61,365 Total interest earned Rs 66,87,046 EPF maturity amount Rs 1,01,48,411

Under these assumptions, the employee could accumulate approximately Rs 1 crore in around 29 years. While the government reviews the EPF interest rate annually, in this calculation we are assuming that the rate remains unchanged at 8.25% throughout the period.

We have also assumed an average 6% annual increase in salary, which in turn would increase your EPF contribution every year.

(Disclaimer: Times of India does not give any personal finance or stock market investment advice. Always consult an expert before taking investment decisions)

Being a crorepati and accumulating a corpus of over Rs 1 crore is often a financial goal for money. But when you are thinking of SIPs, mutual funds, stock markets, ETFs, gold, silver, one quiet savings instrument may lead you to the coveted gold, building a crore plus corpus in less than 30 years.The Employees’ Provident Fund (EPF) serves as a long-term savings avenue, helping employees build a retirement corpus through regular contributions and the power of compounding. Contributions are made by both the employee and employer, subject to the applicable EPF rules.As an employee’s salary grows during their working life, the amount going towards EPF can also rise from the minimum monthly contribution of Rs 1,800.Over time, the interest earned on the accumulated balance earns interest, allowing compounding to steadily increase your retirement savings. With regular contributions maintained over a long period, an employee can potentially build an EPF corpus of Rs 1 crore or more.Of course, the time required to accumulate a Rs 1 crore through EPF depends largely on the monthly contribution and the number of years for which the money remains invested.A longer contribution period gives compounding more time to work, meaning even smaller regular contributions can eventually grow into a substantial corpus. Similarly, higher contributions from the employee and employer can help build a sizable retirement fund over a shorter period.The calculation can then show how long it could take to reach the Rs 1 crore mark.Every contribution made to EPF continues to earn interest during the investment period. As the employee’s salary increases, the contributions made by both the employee and employer also rise.As a result, the amount added to the EPF account changes from year to year rather than remaining the same throughout the 29-year period.Under these assumptions, the employee’s total EPF contribution would amount to around Rs 34.61 lakh, while the interest accumulated over the period would be approximately Rs 66.85 lakh. Combined, the contributions and interest would result in a retirement corpus of over Rs 1 crore, according to the SBI Securities calculator.The final amount in the EPF account can, however, vary depending on factors such as the employee’s actual salary, annual salary increases, contribution levels, periods without employment, the employer’s contribution and the EPF interest rate applicable during the 29-year period.Maintaining a 6% annual increase in basic salary over several decades can make a substantial difference to the eventual corpus. If the salary rises at a higher or lower rate, the corresponding EPF contributions and the final retirement corpus would also change.Also, if you start at a basic salary of Rs 25,000 at the age of say 22, the final corpus at the time of retirement would be much higher. The 29 year period is the time it would take for your EPF corpus to cross the Rs 1 crore mark with all conditions mentioned above staying the same.Can an employer deduct its own EPF contribution from an employee’s wages? No. An employer is not permitted to recover its share of EPF contribution by deducting the amount from an employee’s wages. Such a deduction constitutes a criminal offence, according to an ET report.Can an employee contribute more than the statutory EPF rate of 12%? Yes. In addition to the mandatory contribution, an EPF member can make voluntary contributions.
Article Summary: EPF serves as a long-term savings avenue, helping employees build a retirement corpus. Over time, the interest earned on the accumulated balance earns interest, allowing compounding to steadily increase your retirement savings. With regular contributions maintained over a long period, an employee can potentially build an EPF corpus of Rs 1 crore or more.

Article Title: 5-member NCLT bench stays Subhash Chandra Rs 6.5 crore repayment order
Article Text:
NCLT stayed its earlier order allowing Subhash Chandra to settle his personal insolvency proceedings

NEW DELHI: National Company Law Tribunal (NCLT) on Tuesday stayed its earlier order allowing Zee Group founder Subhash Chandra to settle his personal insolvency proceedings by paying Rs 6.25 crore as against admitted claims of Rs 22,006.57 crore and also restrained him from alienating his assets. A five-member special bench headed by tribunal chief Anupinder Singh Grewal said there was no clear majority view on the repayment plan and put on hold the earlier order.The litigation has remained inconclusive over the last one year because of dissenting orders. A two-member NCLT bench had delivered a split verdict in Sept 2025, with one member approving the repayment plan while the other rejected it, citing irregularities in the admission of claims and voting.The case was referred to a third member, who on Aug 25 approved the repayment plan, subject to exclusion of certain disputed claims and reallocation of their share among eligible creditors. But the third member’s order was then found to have not produced a clear majority when read with the earlier split verdict, and this led to the constitution of the five-member special bench.Analysing all three orders passed by different members, the five-member bench said, “It is manifest that as per Section 419 (5) of the Companies Act, 2013, there is no clear majority view capable of being given effect to; therefore, the order dated Aug 25 of the third member Nilesh Sharma, member (judicial), is stayed.We also direct that the personal guarantor shall not alienate any assets whatsoever either directly or indirectly. Let notice be issued to the parties in all the IAs (interim applications). Reply, if any, may be filed before the next date of hearing.” The tribunal posted the case for hearing after three weeks on Sept 23.The dispute has also reached NCLAT, where dissenting lenders have challenged the repayment plan and the solicitor general sought a day’s time to decide whether the lenders wanted to proceed with the appeal.
Article Summary: National Company Law Tribunal (NCLT) on Tuesday stayed its earlier order allowing Zee Group founder Subhash Chandra to settle his personal insolvency proceedings. A five-member special bench headed by tribunal chief Anupinder Singh Grewal said there was no clear majority view on the repayment plan and put on hold the earlier order.

Article Title: GST inflow rises by double digits 3rd month in a row
Article Text:
GST collections grew at double-digit rates for the third straight month on the back of a 29% jump

NEW DELHI: GST collections grew at double-digit rates for the third straight month on the back of a 29% jump in the mop-up from imports in Aug, while revenue from domestic transactions was up 9.3%.Latest available data estimated GST collections to have risen 14.8% to Rs 1,99,853 crore, with over two-thirds coming from domestic sources, while Rs 62,604 crore came from imports. The collections in Aug relate to transactions in July.The soaring revenue from imports is on account of higher cost of several commodities -- from crude to fertiliser and bullion. At the same time, higher consumption for white goods and automobiles have partly made up for the cut in rates, which took effect last Sept."These collections are a very reliable barometer of the economy since they cover both goods and services consumption across the country. There does not appear to be any slowdown in economic activity and consumption in India, despite the tariff headwinds and the West Asia situation. Considering the fact that collections have shown a marked increase month-on-month despite the rate reductions in Sept 2025 , the GST Council should consider further easing of the input tax credit restrictions , audit rationalisation and reducing compliance burden.This would enable businesses to perform better in an increasingly competitive and complex operating environment," said MS Mani, partner at Deloitte India, a consulting firm. The GST Council is due to meet later this month."The uptick in exports across electronics, mobile phones and automotives is a positive validation of govt's manufacturing-focused policy interventions, signalling that India's positioning in global value chains is strengthening. That said, the concurrent rise in imports points to continuing dependence on external sourcing in certain segments, reinforcing the need for a calibrated policy push towards deeper localisation and import substitution in these sectors," said Saurabh Agrawal, partner at EY India, another consulting firm.During Aug, refunds were up nearly 68% to Rs 31,795 crore. This meant that net collections were 8.3% higher at Rs 1,68,057 crore. Manipur (down 38%), Jharkhand (-22%) and Chhattisgarh (-18%), however, were among states where collections fell, while Assam (97%), Gujarat (28%) and Mizoram (22%) led the growth charts.
Article Summary: Latest available data estimated GST collections to have risen 14.8% to Rs 1,99,853 crore. Over two-thirds coming from domestic sources, while Rs 62,604 crore came from imports. The soaring revenue from imports is on account of higher cost of several commodities -- from crude to fertiliser and bullion.

Article Title: Sun Pharma offers US cheaper drug supply
Article Text:
Sun Pharma has offered Most Favoured Nation (MFN) pricing to US Medicaid programme

New Delhi: Facing the threat of potential tariffs, India’s largest drug firm, Sun Pharma has offered Most Favoured Nation (MFN) pricing to US Medicaid programme under an agreement with the Trump administration. MFN pricing typically ensures that a buyer procures at the lowest price, compared to other developed nations.The deal provides a playbook for domestic pharma companies looking to expand their sales in the US, the world’s largest market, by building their portfolio of innovative or speciality drugs. The agreement signed on Aug 31 recognises Sun Pharma’s investment in the US market by delaying potential Section 232 tariffs on innovative pharmaceutical products for over two years, a company statement said.Under Section 232, US announced a 100% duty on innovative, patented drug imports, while generic medicines imported into the country would face tariffs of 100% from Aug 2028 and 200% a year later. The agreement with the US govt is aimed at prioritising access to affordable medicines for American patients.US is Sun Pharma’s largest market for innovative medicines and a cornerstone of its long-term growth strategy, generating approximately 27% of its global revenue.Sun Pharma scrip closed over 1% lower at Rs 1,931 on BSE.Analysts said sales of Sun Pharma’s innovative drugs in US are around $1 billion, and are expected to increase to about $3 billion, following acquisition of Organon.“The agreement is a politically astute decision that needed to be made, while it also removes the overhang of tariffs. With the Organon deal, the company’s scale would increase significantly. There would be hardly any impact on earnings due to the reduction in prices’’, Vishal Manchanda, analyst at Systematix Group told TOI.The development comes at an important time as the company continues to shift its US business beyond generics towards higher-value specialty and innovative medicines. Sun Pharma initially built its US presence on generics, followed by an increasing emphasis on innovative and specialty medicines. The company ranks second by prescriptions in US dermatology and continues to expand across dermatology and immunology, cutaneous oncology and ophthalmology.The company joined eight pharma majors, which signed agreements on Aug 31 at the White House to reduce prices on drugs that treat numerous costly, chronic and even rare diseases, including hemophilia, Parkinson’s disease, macular degeneration, glaucoma, liver disease, skin conditions, and various forms of cancer, according to a White House statement.Rick Ascroft, North America CEO, Sun Pharma, who represented the company at the White House, said: “The United States is a key area of investment and expansion for Sun Pharma across clinical development, sales and marketing, and both active pharmaceutical ingredients (APIs) and finished products manufacturing’’. Further terms of the agreements remain confidential.The agreement also includes a commitment to strengthen the US supply chain by contributing APIs to the Strategic Active Pharmaceutical Ingredients Reserve (SAPIR) to reduce reliance on foreign nations and ensure the US builds a stockpile. Sun Pharma will contribute 71.4 tons of clindamycin and 6.8 tons of doxycycline; both antibiotics to treat bacterial infections, to the SAPIR. The latest agreements bring the total number of pharma manufacturers with MFN deals to 26, covering 89% of branded drug market in the US.
Article Summary: Facing the threat of potential tariffs, Sun Pharma has offered Most Favoured Nation (MFN) pricing to US Medicaid programme. MFN pricing typically ensures that a buyer procures at the lowest price, compared to other developed nations. The deal provides a playbook for domestic pharma companies looking to expand their sales in the US.

Article Title: TCS pips Accenture to take over Best Buy's India GCC ops
Article Text:
TCS pulled ahead of Accenture in the final leg of the race to take over the India GCC operations of US consumer electronics retailer Best Buy

BENGALURU: Indian IT firms are stepping up their global capability centre (GCC) playbook. TCS pulled ahead of Accenture in the final leg of the race to take over the India GCC operations of US consumer electronics retailer Best Buy, people familiar with the matter told TOI.Best Buy floated a request for proposal (RFP) for a technology services engagement, and TCS won the mandate based on competitive pricing and aggressive service-level agreements (SLAs) and productivity benefits, sources said. Wipro is learnt to have been part of the initial shortlist.Best Buy's India GCC, based in Bengaluru, has around 600 employees. The five-year deal, covering the GCC operations and broader technology services offering, including data, analytics and AI, is estimated to be worth around Rs 2,000 crore, people in the know said. Emails sent to TCS, Accenture, Wipro and Best Buy did not elicit a response till press time.The deal would deepen TCS's longstanding relationship with Best Buy, spanning technology services and digital transformation. Phil Fersht, CEO of HFS Research, estimated the existing TCS relationship with Best Buy at $75-$100 million in annual revenue, while stressing that there is no publicly disclosed contract value.Best Buy set up a 70,000-sft technology centre in Bengaluru in 2024 to accelerate its digital transformation. The centre was envisaged as an innovation hub spanning digital strategy, product management, design, engineering, infrastructure and operations."It's our intention to really make the Best Buy India hub the heart of innovation around how we're going to use mobile and AI platforms. We're going to be building and ramping up teams very actively in those areas," Brian Tilzer, then chief digital, analytics and technology officer at Best Buy, had told TOI in 2024.The India centre has become more strategic as Best Buy steps up investments in AI and digital commerce. The retailer reported revenue of $41.7 billion in FY2026, compared with $41.5 billion a year earlier, while comparable sales rose 0.5%. Computing and mobile phones drove growth, partly offset by declines in home theatre and appliances.
Article Summary: TCS pulled ahead of Accenture in the final leg of the race to take over the India GCC operations of US consumer electronics retailer Best Buy. Wipro is learnt to have been part of the initial shortlist. The five-year deal is estimated to be worth around Rs 2,000 crore.

Article Title: Soota to deploy Rs 1,300 cr stake-sale proceeds in healthcare ventures
Article Text:
Ashok Soota, Chairman and chief mentor, Happiest Minds Technologies

BengaluruAshok Soota plans to deploy a substantial part of the Rs 1,300 crore proceeds from his stake sale in Happiest Minds to ITC Infotech into his healthcare ventures, Skan Research Trust and Happiest Health, as he seeks to scale initiatives focused on ageing, neurological research and healthcare delivery, said Venkatraman Narayanan, managing director and CFO of Happiest Minds.Soota was unavailable for comment after the transaction.Narayanan said Soota was looking to pare his investment in Happiest Minds to fund Skan and Happiest Health, which he wants to build as part of his legacy.“The requirements charted out in both entities are quite massive. Skan has just set up its first campus, which started operations last week, and he now wants to scale that up to a 2-lakh-sft campus. They have already signed up premises and facilities that need to be converted into physical hospitals. So, just the capital investment required in these entities over the next five to six months, which has already been committed, is substantial,” Narayanan told TOI.Skan recently opened its first 22,000-sft campus in Attibele, Bengaluru, focused on ageing and neurological research. The initiative has partnerships with the University of Cambridge, Quadram Institute of Biosciences and Wellcome Sanger Institute.Soota has previously committed Rs 200 crore towards Skan, with the Centre for Brain Research at IISc and St John’s Geriatric Centre in Bengaluru among its key partners. Some funding will also go to IIT-Roorkee and Nimhans.Through Skan, Soota has created an overarching holding trust and a medical research trust designed to co-exist and operate in perpetuity. “It was very clear that he wanted to leave that as part of his legacy and build a business that could make a difference,” Narayanan said.Meanwhile, Happiest Health is expanding its diagnostics and clinics footprint, with 12 healthcare centres ranging from 30,000 sft to 80,000 sft, Narayanan said.Soota, who founded Happiest Minds 15 years ago, had previously sold shares through block deals. The latest transaction provides him with a strategic route to partially exit the company while retaining a stake in the merged entity.Under the transaction, around 22.1% of Soota’s holding is being transferred to ITC Infotech for cash in two stages. He will retain around 7.55% in the merged entity following the proposed merger.Narayanan said Soota’s decision was not driven by concerns over Happiest Minds’ future or the impact of AI on technology services valuations. “So we looked at the options available to us and what we have ultimately chosen,” he said.The merger with ITC Infotech is aimed at creating a larger technology services platform and accelerating Happiest Minds’ ambition of becoming a $1-billion company.Joseph Anantharaju, executive vice-chairman of Happiest Minds, said the technology services industry was undergoing a structural shift, with AI becoming central to customer strategies, alongside vendor consolidation and growing demand for broader capabilities and scale.
Article Summary: Ashok Soota plans to deploy a substantial part of the Rs 1,300 crore proceeds from his stake sale in Happiest Minds to ITC Infotech into his healthcare ventures. He wants to scale initiatives focused on ageing, neurological research and healthcare delivery. Skan recently opened its first 22,000-sft campus in Attibele, Bengaluru.

Article Title: India’s ER&D revenue to cross $100 bn by 2030: Nasscom
Article Text: shilpa.phadnis@timesofindia.comBengaluruIndia is emerging as a new growth engine for the global engineering, research and development (ER&D) industry, with its ER&D services revenue expected to cross $100 billion by 2030 from an estimated $63 billion in FY26.The growth comes as global ER&D spending is projected to reach $2.48–2.50 trillion by 2030, expanding at a compound annual growth rate (CAGR) of 8–9% between CY24 and CY30. Technological disruption, coupled with a sharper focus on innovation and value creation, is opening up new areas of demand for ER&D services.A significant part of this shift is being driven by artificial intelligence (AI), which is moving beyond productivity-focused use cases and becoming increasingly embedded across the engineering and product development lifecycle.Physical AI is emerging as the next major frontier for engineering, research and development (ER&D), creating new opportunities for Indian ER&D providers to move beyond traditional engineering services and take greater ownership of intelligent products and systems, according to Nasscom.In a study titled Physical AI – Redefining ER&D Opportunity for India, Nasscom said demand for Physical AI-led engineering services is likely to evolve in three waves, beginning with intelligent products and operations and eventually moving towards autonomous systems.The first wave is expected to centre on embedded AI, connected equipment, predictive maintenance and intelligent inspection, as enterprises integrate AI into existing products and industrial systems. This will be followed by greater adoption of simulation, virtual engineering and intelligent manufacturing as companies move from experimentation to production.Over the longer term, autonomous systems could emerge as the largest opportunity as barriers related to safety, reliability, computing and real-world deployment are progressively addressed, the study said.For India, the opportunity is significant as the country already has strong capabilities across AI, embedded systems, automotive and industrial ER&D, simulation and data engineering.“India’s ER&D growth will be shaped by how effectively we combine our engineering depth with AI to take on greater ownership of global product development. Physical AI adds an important new dimension to this opportunity,” said Rajesh Nambiar, president, Nasscom.“India has the engineering talent, domain expertise and scale to play a much larger role across this lifecycle. The opportunity now is to move further towards systems-led engineering and co-creation of intelligent products and platforms,” he said.The shift could also create revenue pools beyond traditional engineering services. Nasscom said ER&D providers could explore models such as AI-as-a-Service, Robotics-as-a-Service, leasing models, autonomous platforms and agentic deployments.Indian ER&D providers can build on existing engineering capabilities to develop reusable intellectual property and capture opportunities across the Physical AI lifecycle, from product development and simulation to deployment and operations.However, realising the opportunity will require companies to invest in cross-disciplinary talent and build strategic partnerships across technology platforms and ecosystems. Domain-specific AI models will also be critical to translate real-world data into systems and processes that continuously improve.The emergence of Physical AI could therefore shift India’s ER&D opportunity from executing engineering projects for global companies to becoming a critical engineering layer connecting AI intelligence with the physical world.The development comes as global ER&D spending rises amid technological disruption and a growing focus among enterprises on innovation, product differentiation and value creation. AI is increasingly moving beyond productivity use cases and becoming embedded across the product and engineering lifecycle, creating new areas of demand for ER&D providers.
Article Summary: India is emerging as a new growth engine for the global engineering, research and development (ER&D) industry. Its ER&D services revenue is expected to cross $100 billion by 2030 from an estimated $63 billion in FY26. The growth comes as global ER & D spending is projected to reach $2.48–2.50 trillion by 2030.

Article Title: Petrol and Diesel demand rises, LPG down
Article Text:
Petrol usage increased by a notable 7.9 percent compared to last year, while diesel saw a rise of 6.5 percent during the same timeframe.

NEW DELHI: Consumption of petrol increased 7.9 percent year-on-year in Aug, while diesel registered a growth of 6.5 percent, according to provisional data released by Petroleum Planning and Analysis Cell (PPAC) Tuesday.Petrol sales increased to 3.8 million tonnes (MT) from 3.5 MT in the same month last year, while diesel consumption rose to 7 MT from 6.6 MT, data showed. Petrol and diesel consumption had registered year-on-year growth of 9.7 percent and 10.7 percent, respectively, in July.Diesel is widely used by transport vehicles for passenger and freight movement, besides being used in the agricultural sector. Erratic monsoon conditions due to El Nino boosted demand for diesel for irrigation.LPG demand, however, fell 16.2 percent to 2.4 MT from 2.9 MT a year earlier, continuing a trend seen during the summer months. ATF consumption rose marginally by 1.4 percent to 7.2 lakh tonnes from 7.1 lakh tonnes.Cumulative petrol consumption during Apr-Aug in the current financial year increased 6.5 percent to 18.9 MT, while diesel consumption rose 4.3 percent to 40.6 MT. In contrast, LPG consumption declined 15.9 percent to 11.3 MT from 13.4 MT during the corresponding period of 2025-26.
Article Summary: Petrol usage increased by a notable 7.9 percent compared to last year, while diesel saw a rise of 6.5 percent during the same timeframe. LPG demand, however, fell 16.2 percent to 2.4 MT from 2.9 MT a year earlier.
